data.why: The repo ships small bundled test-fixture images (BBBC005 focus fixtures, FocusNet held-out examples) and a growth video; an evidence-map/endpoint CSV pair referencing those images by exact filename lets the browser reach the full plate-evidence workflow without needing well-ID-coded filenames.

goals: Link a plate map and an independent plate-reader endpoint to microscopy images by well or evidence ID and compute the apparent treatment effect
Audit image QC (focus, illumination, segmentation coverage) and recalculate the effect after excluding failed images
Run leave-one-replicate-out sensitivity analysis and a treatment-label permutation test to see whether the effect survives
Compare the microscopy-derived effect against the independent plate-reader/flow-cytometry endpoint for concordance
Read Parallax's cautious evidence verdict (robust, quality-sensitive, replicate-sensitive, modality-discordant, underpowered, or inconclusive) and export the evidence report
Upload a brightfield/phase-contrast microscopy video and review the automatic cell observation, tracking, and event timeline

review.summary: The tree states Parallax's purpose well (stress-testing a microscopy treatment effect, plus a separate video observer), its tasks are at the right depth, and 10 sampled screens largely support it; one citation (t5 on 019) is wrong. It needs fixes before filing: the generic plate heatmap, position-matching and FocusNet paths, plus a permutation task, are missing; the fixture data left the QC-adjusted and LORO results degenerate; and the video branch could not be reproduced on replay.
